mission.3.step1.title: The starting point
mission.3.step1.explain: You have a report folder and a two-commit history on the main lane.
mission.3.step2.title: A desk for the “figures” AI
mission.3.step2.explain: A worktree is one more folder linked to the same repository. The AI works there on its own branch, without touching your folder.
mission.3.step2.hint: Start with git worktree add, then the path of the new folder, then -b and the branch name.
mission.3.step3.title: A desk for the “summary” AI
mission.3.step3.explain: Same idea for a second AI: another folder, another branch, the same repository.
mission.3.step3.hint: Same command, with ../rpt-ia-resume and the branch ia/resume.
mission.3.step4.title: See where things stand
mission.3.step4.explain: git worktree list shows each folder and the branch it has open.
mission.3.outro: Three folders, one history. Each moves forward on its own lane without getting in the others' way.
explain.worktree.add: A new folder “{path}” is opened on branch {branch}. The repository stays single.
explain.worktree.list: The list shows each folder and the branch it has open.
explain.commit: A snapshot of the project is saved on the {branch} lane.
explain.add: {file} is staged: it will be part of the next snapshot.
explain.branch: A new lane {name} starts from the current commit.
explain.switch: This folder now works on the {name} lane.
explain.squash: {n} commits are folded into one, easier to read.
explain.squash.one: {n} commit stays as it is: there is nothing to fold.
error.branchInUse: Branch {name} is already open in folder {path}. A branch can live in only one folder at a time.
error.pushRejected: Rejected: the online version has moved on. Fetch the changes first (pull).
error.worktreeDirty: This folder has unsaved changes: it can't be removed.
error.nothingToCommit: Nothing to save: no file is staged.
error.mergeConflict: Conflict: both lanes changed the same file, {file}.
diff.conflict.noDetail: This scenario does not detail the content; in a real project Git would show you the conflicting lines.
puzzle.label: Challenge {n} of 10
puzzle.4.title: Three “wip” into one
puzzle.4.prompt: The AI left three “wip” commits. Fold them into one before sharing.
puzzle.4.goal: A single clean commit on the ia/chiffres lane.
puzzle.4.why.reset: reset --hard erases the work instead of grouping it.
puzzle.4.why.revert: revert adds an undo commit; it doesn't group anything.
puzzle.4.why.merge: merge brings in another lane; it doesn't tidy this one.
puzzle.4.takeaway: rebase -i lets you fold (squash) several commits into one before sharing.
tree.tip: Click a file: modified, then staged, then clean. A folder opens on click. The + adds a file.
diff.title: The diff: what changed
diff.readonly: nothing is changed: we only look
diff.sentence.branches: Here is what assistant 1 changed on its lane, compared with main. Nothing is merged yet.
diff.sentence.work: What you changed but have not staged with git add yet. New files (U) do not show up here.
diff.sentence.staged: What is staged in the index: exactly what will go into the next commit.
diff.empty.untracked: A new file does not show in git diff until it is staged. Run first: git add {file}
mission.3.stepDiff.title: Review its work with diff
mission.3.stepDiff.explain: git diff compares two lanes: removed lines in red, added lines in green. Nothing is changed.
mission.3.stepDiff.hint: Type git diff, then main, then ia/resume.
mission.7.title: A readable history
mission.6.bubbleA: An AI assistant opened MR !42 on its branch ia/graphiques. You are in the middle of your own work. Let’s review its MR the classic way: by switching branches.
mission.6.bubbleB: Same MR, another method: we open a second folder just for the review. Keep an eye on your desk during the whole mission.
mission.6.outroA: It works, but your desk was disturbed during the whole review, and you had to remember stash pop.
mission.6.outroB: Your work never moved. The review folder takes one command to create and is thrown away afterwards.
mission.6.a1.title: Look at your work in progress
mission.6.a1.ex: Before switching branches, check what is in progress.
mission.6.a1.after: Two modified files (M): your work is not saved yet.
mission.6.a2.title: Put your work away
mission.6.a2.ex: Set your work aside so you can switch branches without carrying it along or losing it.
mission.6.a2.after: Your M files are gone from the folder: they are put away in the stash, in zone ③.
mission.6.a2.note: Your work is hidden, not lost.
mission.6.a3.title: Fetch the MR’s branch
mission.6.a3.ex: Download what is online, without touching your folder.
mission.6.a3.after: The MR’s lane now exists on your side, as origin/ia/graphiques.
mission.6.a4.title: Open the MR’s branch
mission.6.a4.ex: Your folder takes the content of the MR’s branch.
mission.6.a4.after: Your folder changed content: the graphiques/ folder appeared. The thread now runs to the blue lane.
mission.6.a4.note: Same folder, different content: you are no longer on main.
mission.6.a5.title: Review with diff
mission.6.a5.ex: Compare the MR’s branch with main: only what the MR brings.
mission.6.a5.after: Two added files (A) and one modified (M). Open the diff screen to read line by line.
mission.6.a6.title: Approve the MR
mission.6.a6.ex: The review is done: give your approval online.
mission.6.a6.after: The MR is approved. It can be merged into main.
mission.6.a7.title: Go back and bring your work out
mission.6.a7.ex: Back to main, then bring the stashed work back.
mission.6.a7.after: You are back on main and your two M files are back. Without stash pop, they would have stayed hidden.
mission.6.b1.title: Fetch the MR’s branch
mission.6.b1.ex: Download what is online, without touching your folder.
mission.6.b1.after: The MR’s lane exists on your side, as origin/ia/graphiques. Your M files did not move.
mission.6.b2.title: Open a review desk
mission.6.b2.ex: A second folder, open on the MR’s branch. No stash needed.
mission.6.b2.after: A new folder revue-mr-42 appeared, linked to the blue lane. Your desk is untouched, at 60%: you now work in the review.
mission.6.b2.note: Your desk did not move: your M files are still there.
mission.6.b3.title: Review with diff
mission.6.b3.ex: In the review folder, compare the MR’s branch with main.
mission.6.b3.after: Two added files (A) and one modified (M). Open the diff screen to read line by line.
mission.6.b4.title: Approve, then merge
mission.6.b4.ex: Give your approval, then the MR is merged into main, online.
mission.6.b4.after: The MR is merged on origin: origin/main moved forward. Your local main has not moved yet.
mission.6.b4.note: Merged online: you will need to fetch it.
mission.6.b5.title: Remove the review desk
mission.6.b5.ex: The review folder has done its job: remove it.
mission.6.b5.after: The review folder is gone. The ia/graphiques branch still exists in the .git.
mission.6.b6.title: Update main
mission.6.b6.ex: In your desk, bring in the merge made online.
mission.6.b6.after: main moved up to the merge, and your two M files are still there: your work was never disturbed.

error.emptyCommand: Type a command first, for example git status.
error.missingSubcommand: git on its own does nothing: add what you want to do, for example git status.
error.missingArgument: {command} needs something more: a name, a file or a commit.
error.notAvailable: The command {name} is not available here yet.
error.outOfScope.clone: git clone makes a full copy of a repository, with its own .git. The game does not simulate it; the Team start shows what it produces.
error.outOfScope.tag: Tags (labels on a commit) are not part of this game.
error.outOfScope.submodule: Submodules (a repository inside another) are not part of this game.
error.outOfScope.config: Git settings are not part of this game.
error.outOfScope.gc: Cleaning up the .git is not part of this game.
error.outOfScope.reflog: The reflog (Git’s logbook of moves) is not part of this game.
error.outOfScope.bisect: git bisect (hunting for the commit that broke something) is not part of this game.
error.outOfScope.mv: Renaming files is not part of this game.
error.outOfScope.clean: git clean (deleting new files) is not part of this game.
error.unknownRevision: Git does not know “{rev}”: neither a branch nor a commit.
error.unknownFile: There is no file {file} in this folder.
error.branchExists: A branch called {name} already exists. Pick another name, or open it with git switch {name}.
error.invalidBranchName: “{name}” cannot be a branch name (no spaces, no “..”, no slash at the end).
error.branchCheckedOut: Branch {name} is open in folder {path}: it cannot be deleted while it is in use.
error.branchNotMerged: Branch {name} holds work that is not merged anywhere. To delete it anyway: git branch -D {name}.
error.limitBranches: The game shows at most {max} branches. Delete or merge one first.
error.limitDesks: The game shows at most {max} folders. Remove one with git worktree remove first.
error.limitCommits: The game shows about {max} commits at most. Start again from a lighter start to go on.
error.worktreeMain: {path} is the original folder: it holds the .git and cannot be removed.
error.switchWouldOverwrite: Your unsaved changes to {files} would be overwritten. Save them (commit) or put them aside (git stash) first.
error.switchNeedsDetach: {rev} is a commit, not a branch. To look at it without a branch: git switch --detach {rev}.
error.mergeWouldOverwrite: Your unsaved changes to {files} are in the way. Save them (commit) or put them aside (git stash) first.
error.stashWouldOverwrite: Bringing back the stash would overwrite your changes to {files}. Save them first.
error.rebaseDirty: Rebase replays commits in this folder: save (commit) or put aside (git stash) your changes to {files} first.
error.rebaseMerges: These commits include a merge: the interactive rebase of the game only works on a straight lane.
error.rebasePlanInvalid: The rebase plan must give one action (pick, reword, squash, fixup, drop) for each of the {n} commits.
error.rebasePlanInvalid.one: The rebase plan must give one action (pick, reword, squash, fixup, drop) for the commit.
error.nothingToRebase: There is no commit to rework here.
error.operationInProgress: A {op} is in progress in this folder. Finish it (resolve the conflict, then git add and git commit, or git rebase --continue) or cancel it with --abort.
error.noOperation: There is no {op} in progress here.
error.useRebaseContinue: A rebase is in progress: after git add, finish with git rebase --continue.
error.conflictUnresolved: {file} is still in conflict. Choose which version to keep first.
error.conflictNotAdded: The conflict on {file} is resolved, but not staged yet: git add {file}.
error.conflictChooseFirst: {file} is in conflict: choose which version to keep (mine, theirs or both) before going on.
error.nothingToStash: Nothing to put aside: no file is modified.
error.stashEmpty: The stash is empty: nothing to bring back.
error.noCommitYet: There is no commit yet: make a first one with git commit.
error.commitMessageMissing: A commit needs a short message: git commit -m "what you did".
error.restoreUntracked: {file} is new: Git has never saved it, so there is no earlier version to bring back.
error.cherryPickMerge: {rev} is a merge commit: the game only copies ordinary commits.
error.cherryPickEmpty: The changes of {rev} are already on this lane: nothing to copy.
error.revertMerge: {rev} is a merge commit: the game only undoes ordinary commits.
warn.detachedHead: Careful: you are on commit {id} without a branch (“detached HEAD”). Commits made here belong to no lane.
warn.detachedCommit: Commit {id} belongs to no branch. Give it one with git switch -c <name> so it is not lost.
warn.checkoutLegacy: git checkout works, but today we write: {modern}.
explain.status: {n} files have changed in this folder; staged for the next commit: {staged}.
explain.status.one: {n} file has changed in this folder; staged for the next commit: {staged}.
explain.status.clean: Nothing to report: the folder matches the last commit of {branch}.
explain.status.op: A {op} is in progress: {n} files are involved.
explain.status.op.one: A {op} is in progress: {n} file is involved.
explain.add.many: {n} files are staged: they will be part of the next snapshot.
explain.add.many.one: {n} file is staged: it will be part of the next snapshot.
explain.add.nothing: Nothing new to stage: these files have not changed.
explain.commit.amend: The last commit is redone with the current content. The old one disappears from the lane.
explain.commit.merge: The merge is saved: the {name} lane now joins {into}.
explain.restore: {file} is back to its saved version. The changes in the folder are thrown away.
explain.restore.staged: {file} leaves the index: it will not be in the next commit. Your changes stay in the folder.
explain.restore.both: {file} leaves the index and goes back to its saved version.
explain.rm: {file} is deleted from the folder (D). The deletion will be saved after git add and git commit.
explain.rm.git: {file} is deleted and the deletion is staged for the next commit.
explain.stash.push: Your changes ({files}) are put aside in the stash. The folder is back to the last commit.
explain.stash.pop: Your changes ({files}) come back out of the stash, into the folder.
explain.stash.apply: Your changes ({files}) are copied back into the folder; they also stay in the stash.
explain.stash.drop: The last entry of the stash is thrown away.
explain.stash.list: The stash of this folder holds {n} entries.
explain.stash.list.one: The stash of this folder holds {n} entry.
explain.stash.conflict: The stash and the lane both changed {file}: choose which version to keep. The entry stays in the stash.
explain.branch.delete: The {name} lane is deleted. Its commits were already merged elsewhere.
explain.branch.forceDelete: The {name} lane is deleted, even though its work was not merged: its commits fade away.
explain.switch.create: A new lane {name} starts here, and this folder now works on it.
explain.switch.track: The online branch {remote} becomes a local branch {name}, and this folder opens it.
explain.switch.detach: This folder now shows commit {id}, without a branch: you can look, but new commits would belong to no lane.
explain.merge.ff: {into} had not moved: it simply catches up with {name} (fast-forward). No merge commit is needed.
explain.merge.upToDate: {into} already contains all the work of {name}: nothing to do.
explain.merge.conflict: {name} and {into} both changed {file}. Git cannot choose for you: pick a version, then git add and git commit.
explain.merge.abort: The merge is cancelled: the folder is back as it was before.
explain.rebase: The commits of {branch} are replayed on top of {name}, as if the work had started from there.
explain.rebase.ff: {branch} simply moves up to {name}: there was nothing to replay.
explain.rebase.upToDate: This lane already starts from the latest commit of {name}: nothing to do.
explain.rebase.interactive: The commits of {branch} are rewritten following your plan.
explain.rebase.conflict: While replaying, {file} was changed on both sides. Choose a version, git add it, then git rebase --continue.
explain.rebase.abort: The rebase is cancelled: the lane is back as it was before.
explain.cherryPick: Commit {rev} is copied onto {branch}: a new commit with the same changes.
explain.cherryPick.conflict: Copying {rev} touches {file}, which was also changed here. Choose a version, then git add and git commit.
explain.cherryPick.abort: The copy is cancelled: the folder is back as it was before.
explain.revert: A new commit undoes the changes of {rev}. The history keeps both: nothing is rewritten.
explain.revert.conflict: Undoing {rev} touches {file}, which changed since. Choose a version, then git add and git commit.
explain.revert.abort: The undo is cancelled: the folder is back as it was before.
explain.reset.soft: {branch} moves back to {rev}. The changes of the removed commits stay staged in the index.
explain.reset.mixed: {branch} moves back to {rev}. Your files keep their changes (M), ready to be redone.
explain.reset.hard: {branch} moves back to {rev}, and the folder too: the later changes are erased.
explain.worktree.addDetached: A new folder “{path}” shows commit {id}, without a branch.
explain.worktree.remove: The folder {path} is removed. The {branch} lane stays in the .git.
explain.worktree.prune: Git tidies up its list of folders. Nothing visible changes.
explain.diff.work: Your changes not staged yet, line by line. New files (U) do not show up here.
explain.diff.work.empty: No change waiting outside the index.
explain.diff.staged: What is staged in the index: exactly what the next commit will contain.
explain.diff.staged.empty: Nothing is staged: the next commit would be empty.
explain.diff.branches: The differences between {a} and {b}. Nothing is changed: we only look.
explain.diff.threeDot: What {b} brings since it left {a}: exactly what a merge request shows.
explain.diff.folder: The differences between {a} and the files of your folder.
explain.diff.folder.empty: Your folder has the same content as {a}.
explain.log: The history of {branch}: {n} commits, newest first.
explain.log.empty: No commit yet: the history is empty.
explain.blame: Each line of {file} with the commit that wrote it. Lines from the AI: {ai} of {n}.
explain.blame.one: Each line of {file} with the commit that wrote it. Lines from the AI: {ai} of {n}.
explain.show: Commit {id} and the files it changed ({n}).
explain.touch: You worked on {file}: it is now modified (M).
explain.create: A new file {file} appears (U): Git does not track it yet.
explain.resolve: For {file}, you keep the version of {side}. Then: git add {file}.
explain.resolve.both: For {file}, you keep both versions, one after the other. Then: git add {file}.
explain.cd: You move to the folder {path} (on {branch}). It becomes the active desk.
home.title: Understand Git
home.intro: Git remembers a project's history and lets several people, or several AI assistants, work side by side without mixing anything up. Here you handle it for real, without ever breaking anything.
home.mission.text: A guided story with a human and AI assistant duo. You follow the steps and the scene reacts to each command.
home.puzzle.text: Short challenges: a starting situation, a goal to reach, a few proposed commands. Only one is right.
home.sandbox.text: An open playground: type commands or click in the scene, undo, start over. Nothing can break.
home.sandbox.meta: Start from scratch or from a ready-made situation
home.resume.title: Pick up where you left off
home.missions.title: The missions
home.missions.hint: This is the recommended order, but nothing is locked: start wherever you like.
home.puzzles.title: The puzzles
home.puzzles.hint: Each challenge earns 1 to 3 stars depending on the number of attempts.
home.fallbackNote: Not translated yet: shown in French
shell.home: Comegitmix, back to the home page
diff.untracked.why: Git only looks at files it already follows. A U file is new: Git does not follow it yet, so git diff skips it. Once staged with git add, it shows up in git diff --staged.
diff.conflict.hint: This file is in conflict: choose which version to keep.
diff.needTwoLanes: Two lanes are needed to compare them.
conflict.title: Conflict on {file}
conflict.why: Both lanes changed this file. Git cannot choose for you: you decide which version to keep.
conflict.next.commit: Next: git add {file}, then git commit to finish.
conflict.next.rebase: Next: git add {file}, then git rebase --continue to carry on.
conflict.none: No file is in conflict in this folder.
log.title: History of {branch}
error.noRemote: There is no online repository named {name} yet.
error.unknownRemote: Unknown online repository: {name}. Here we only know origin and upstream.
error.mrNotApproved: Merge request !{id} must be approved before it is merged.
error.mrConflict: Merge request !{id} cannot be merged online: {file} was changed on both sides.
error.pullDetached: You are not on a branch (detached HEAD): pull does not know which lane to update.
error.pushDetached: You are not on a branch (detached HEAD): push does not know which lane to send.
error.aiNothingToDo: The AI finds no file to work on in {path}.
error.setupSyntax: This setup line cannot be read: {text}
explain.fetch: fetch downloaded what is online ({refs}) without touching your branches or your folder.
explain.pull: pull downloaded {ref} and brought it into {branch}.
explain.pull.upToDate: {branch} was already up to date with {ref}.
explain.pull.conflict: pull downloaded {ref}, but {file} was changed on both sides: choose what to keep, then commit.
explain.push: push sent your commits of {branch} online: {ref} has caught up.
explain.push.new: push created {ref} online with the commits of {branch}.
explain.push.upToDate: Nothing to send: {ref} already has every commit of {branch}.
explain.push.force: push replaced {ref} with your version of {branch}, erasing what was online.
explain.fork: {to} is now your own online copy of {from}.
explain.mr.open: Merge request !{id} is open: {source} asks to be merged into {target}.
explain.mr.approve: Merge request !{id} is approved: it can be merged into {target}.
explain.mr.merge: Merge request !{id} is merged online: {source} joined {target} on origin. Your local branches have not moved yet.
explain.mr.close: Merge request !{id} is closed without being merged.
explain.mr.aiOpen: The AI sent {branch} online and opened merge request !{id} towards {target}.
explain.colleague: A colleague pushed a commit to {ref} ({files}). You will only see it after a fetch or a pull.
explain.ai.commit: The AI worked on {files} and saved its work on {branch} (a commit marked AI).
explain.ai.work: The AI worked on {files}. Nothing is saved yet: look at it with git diff.
warn.forcePush: Careful: you rewrote {ref} online. Anyone who already had it will be lost.
equiv.mr.open: (the merge request !{id} is opened on the site)
equiv.mr.approve: (you approve merge request !{id} on the site)
equiv.mr.merge: (you merge merge request !{id} on the site)

sandbox.help.add: git add <file> (or .): puts the file in the index, the list of what the next commit will save.
sandbox.help.commit: git commit -m "message": takes a photo of the index and adds it to the current lane. -am stages modified files first; --amend redoes the last photo.
sandbox.help.restore: git restore <file>: throws away the changes of a file. git restore --staged <file>: takes it out of the index, the changes stay.
sandbox.help.rm: rm <file>: deletes the file from the folder (letter D). Then git add and git commit record the deletion.
sandbox.help.stash: git stash: puts the work in progress aside (one stash per folder). pop brings it back, apply brings a copy, drop deletes it, list shows it.
sandbox.help.branch: git branch <name>: creates a new lane at the current commit, without going on it. -d deletes a merged branch, -D forces.
sandbox.help.switch: git switch <name>: this folder goes on that lane. git switch -c <name> creates it and goes on it.
sandbox.help.checkout: git checkout: the old way to change branch. It works, but today we write git switch (and git restore for files).
sandbox.help.merge: git merge <name>: brings the work of another lane into the current one. If both changed the same file, Git asks you to choose (conflict). --abort goes back.
sandbox.help.rebase: git rebase <name>: replays your commits on top of another lane, as if you had started from there. git rebase -i HEAD~n lets you squash, reword, reorder or drop them.
sandbox.help.cherry-pick: git cherry-pick <commit>: copies one commit from another lane onto the current one.
sandbox.help.reset: git reset <commit>: moves the current lane back to that commit. --soft keeps the changes staged, --mixed keeps them in the folder, --hard throws them away.
sandbox.help.revert: git revert <commit>: adds a new commit that undoes that one. History is not rewritten: safe on a shared branch.
sandbox.help.worktree: git worktree add ../<folder> -b <branch>: opens a new folder on its own lane, sharing the same .git. list shows the folders, remove closes one.
sandbox.help.diff: git diff: your changes not staged yet. --staged: what the next commit will save. git diff <a> <b>: the difference between two lanes.
sandbox.help.log: git log: the list of commits of the current lane, newest first, with the AI's commits marked.
sandbox.help.blame: git blame <file>: who wrote each line of the file, and in which commit (human or AI).
sandbox.help.show: git show <commit>: what a commit changed.
sandbox.help.fetch: git fetch: downloads what is new online without touching your folders (dashed origin/… chips).
sandbox.help.pull: git pull: fetch, then merge the online version into your lane.
sandbox.help.push: git push: sends your lane online. Refused if someone pushed before you: pull first. -u origin <branch> the first time.
sandbox.help.remote: git remote -v: the online repositories this project knows.
sandbox.help.fork: fork: on the hosting site, makes your own online copy (origin) of the original project (upstream).
sandbox.help.cd: cd ../<folder>: you now work in that folder (it becomes 100 % visible).
sandbox.help.ls: ls: lists the files of the current folder.
sandbox.help.clear: clear: empties the terminal. The scene does not change.
sandbox.help.help: help: the list of commands. help <command>: its short card.
sandbox.why.status: Git compares three things: the last commit, the index and the folder. status tells you where each changed file stands, so you know what the next commit will contain.
sandbox.why.add: Git does not save everything you touched: you choose. The index is a waiting room; only what is in it goes into the next commit. Each folder has its own index.
sandbox.why.commit: A commit is a photo of the whole project at a moment, with a message. It is added to the lane of the current folder; the other lanes do not move.
sandbox.why.restore: restore puts back the version of the index (or of the last commit). It is the way to say “forget what I did to this file”.
sandbox.why.rm: Deleting a file is a change like any other: Git notes it (D) and records it at the next commit.
sandbox.why.stash: The stash is a drawer kept in .git, shared by every folder: you put your unfinished work in it to have a clean folder (to change branch, to pull), then you take it back.
sandbox.why.branch: A branch is just a name that points to a commit. Creating one costs nothing: it is a new lane where you can try without disturbing main.
sandbox.why.switch: A folder is on one lane at a time. switch changes the files of the folder to match the other lane. Git refuses if that would overwrite changes not saved.
sandbox.why.checkout: checkout did too many things at once (change branch, restore files). Git split it into switch and restore, which are easier to read.
sandbox.why.merge: Merging joins two lanes: Git takes the work done on each side since they separated. When both sides changed the same file, a human has to decide.
sandbox.why.rebase: Rebase rewrites your commits as if you had started later: the history becomes a straight line. Because the commits are new, avoid it on a lane others already use.
sandbox.why.cherry-pick: Sometimes you want one commit, not the whole lane: cherry-pick copies just that one (it gets a new identity).
sandbox.why.reset: reset moves the lane label backwards. The later commits are no longer on the lane; with --hard the changes of the folder are lost too.
sandbox.why.revert: Undoing by adding is the polite way when others already have your commits: nobody's history is rewritten.
sandbox.why.worktree.add: A worktree is a second folder on the same repository: each folder has its lane, its files and its index, but there is only one .git. That is how several AIs work in parallel without stepping on each other.
sandbox.why.worktree.list: Every folder opened with git worktree shares the same .git: list shows them all with their lane.
sandbox.why.worktree.remove: Removing a worktree closes the folder; the lane and its commits stay in the .git. Git refuses if the folder holds unsaved changes.
sandbox.why.diff: diff shows the lines removed and added. Untracked files (U) are not in git diff: Git does not follow them yet.
sandbox.why.log: The log is the story of a lane: each commit with its author. AI commits are marked so you always know who did what.
sandbox.why.blame: blame is useful to know where a line comes from before changing it, especially when an AI wrote part of the file.
sandbox.why.show: Each commit remembers what it changed: show opens it like a diff.
sandbox.why.fetch: fetch only updates what your repository knows about origin. Your folders and lanes do not move: you decide later what to bring in.
sandbox.why.pull: pull is fetch + merge: you bring the team's work into your lane. If someone changed the same file, it is a conflict to resolve.
sandbox.why.push: push publishes your lane for the team. Git refuses when the online lane moved ahead: you would erase someone's work.
sandbox.why.fork: A fork is your own copy of someone else's project, online. You work there, then propose your changes with a merge request.
sandbox.why.cd: Each folder is a desk: the active one is fully visible, the others fade. Typed commands act on the active folder.
sandbox.why.click: Clicking a file plays a step of the usual cycle: you change it (M), you stage it (git add), and the next click takes it back.
sandbox.why.create: A new file is untracked (U): Git sees it but does not follow it until you git add it.
sandbox.why.resolve: You chose a version for the conflicted file. Git still waits for git add on it, then git commit to finish the merge.
sandbox.why.ai: An AI on its own lane and in its own folder can work without touching your files. Its commits are marked AI: review them with git diff before merging.
sandbox.why.assistant: Each new assistant gets its lane (ia/…) and its folder, created with git worktree add. That is the recipe to have several AIs in parallel.
sandbox.why.ai-mr: A merge request is a proposal: the lane is online, the team reviews it, approves it, then merges it on the site.
sandbox.why.colleague: Others push too. Their work is online, not on your machine yet: git fetch or git pull to get it. A push before that is refused.
sandbox.why.mr.approve: Approving says “I reviewed it, it can go in”. The merge itself comes next.
sandbox.why.mr.merge: The merge happens online, on origin. Your machine only sees it after a git pull.
shell.docsTitle: The Git command cards, in a new tab
docs.title: The commands, in plain words
docs.intro: One card per command: what it is for, what it does in the game, an example and the traps to avoid. Written for people who work with developers without being one.
docs.officialNote: More complete, but written for developers.
error.glabMissing: glab is GitLab’s command line tool. In the game it handles merge requests: type glab mr create, glab mr list, glab mr approve <number>…
error.glabOnlyMr: In the game, glab only handles merge requests (glab mr …): “{sub}” is not one of them.
error.glabMissingAction: glab mr needs an action: create, list, view, approve, merge or close.
error.glabOption: The game does not know the glab option {option}. To create an MR: glab mr create --fill, or -t "title" and -b <target branch>.
error.mrPushFirst: The lane {branch} is not online yet: send it first with git push -u origin {branch}, or let glab do it with glab mr create --fill.
error.mrAlreadyOpen: A merge request is already open for {branch}: !{id}.
error.mrNoneForBranch: No open merge request for the lane {branch}. Give its number: glab mr approve 42.
explain.mr.create: Merge request !{id} is open online: {source} asks to join {target}. The team can now review it.
explain.mr.list: {n} merge requests are waiting for a review or a merge: {ids}.
explain.mr.list.one: {n} merge request is waiting for a review or a merge: {ids}.
explain.mr.view.open: Merge request !{id} proposes to bring {source} into {target}. It is waiting for a review.
explain.mr.view.approved: Merge request !{id} ({source} → {target}) is approved: it can be merged.
explain.mr.view.closed: Merge request !{id} ({source} → {target}) was closed without being merged.
sandbox.help.glab: glab mr …: merge requests from the terminal, with GitLab’s tool. create (--fill) opens one for your lane, list and view show them, approve, merge and close act on one by its number.
error.notARepo: fatal: this folder is not a Git repository (yet). Type git init to make it one.
explain.init: git init created the hidden .git folder in {path}: that is where Git will keep every snapshot. Your {n} files are there, but Git does not track them yet (U). The {branch} lane is waiting for its first commit.
explain.init.again: {path} is already a Git repository: git init changes nothing (Git answers “Reinitialized existing Git repository”).
error.ghOnlyRepoCreate: gh is GitHub’s command line tool. In the game it creates the online repository: gh repo create <name> --public, or with --source=. --push to do everything at once.
error.ghOption: The game does not know the gh option {option}. Possible options: --public, --private, --source=., --push.
error.ghRepoExists: This project already has an online repository origin: no need to create another one ({name}).
error.ghPushNeedsSource: --push sends your local repository: add --source=. to say which one.
explain.gh.create: The repository {name} now exists on GitHub, empty, at {url}. Your local repository does not know it yet: link them with git remote add origin {url}.
explain.gh.createLinked: The repository {name} is created on GitHub and linked under the name origin. It is still empty: git push -u origin main will send your commits there.
explain.gh.createPush: In one command: the repository {name} is created on GitHub, linked under the name origin, and the {branch} lane is sent there. Your project is online.
error.remoteNotCreated: No online repository exists yet for {name}. Create it on GitHub first (gh repo create <name>), then link it. In real life Git would accept the address and only complain at the first push.
error.remoteSubcommand: In the game, git remote lists (git remote -v) or links an online repository (git remote add origin <address>): “{sub}” is not one of them.
explain.remote.add: Your local repository now knows {name}: it is the short name of {url}. Nothing is sent yet, that is what git push does.
repo.origin.pending: Created on GitHub, empty. Your repository does not know it yet: git remote add origin <address>.
repo.origin.empty: Linked to your repository, but still empty: git push will send your commits there.
repo.noGit.desc: This is an ordinary folder: no .git, so no snapshot is possible. git init turns it into a repository.
